subject: Packaging and commercial follow-up: Optimize toolkit pilot & technical boundaries
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@lumensoft.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Optimize toolkit — pilot packaging and recommended technical guardrails

Hi Sarah,

Great to meet last week — thanks for the time. Per our conversation, I wanted to outline a conservative packaging proposal for the Optimize toolkit pilot and call out the technical guidance we expect to pair with the credits.

Commercial sketch (pilot):
- 3-month pilot scoped to your ingestion and summarization route (~200M tokens/month).
- 25,000 pilot credits (applied against token units / optimizer usage) + one week of free inference engineering support during ramp.
- If you hit >75% of the throughput target in month 2, we’ll apply a one-time additional 10k credit top-up.

Technical guidance we’ll include (why this matters):
- Batching: We expect diminishing returns beyond batch sizes that push p99 latency > 600ms; for synchronous summarization workflows we recommend a target batch window of 40–80ms with dynamic batching enabled.
- KV cache: For your user-session workload (many short sessions), we should instrument prefix hit-rate early. If KV hit-rate is >35% we can reduce peak GPU load by ~22% via prefix caching.
- Quantization: We recommend int8 for the base model in production for cost savings, but only after a controlled eval: use per-layer calibration on a representative prompt set. For short contexts (<128 tokens), int8 shows minimal quality degradation on our benchmarks; with long contexts we may hold to int16 for select shards.

I’ve attached the pricing worksheet and a short KV cache latency note. If this looks good I’ll send an updated one-pager and a DocuSign for the pilot SOW + flex terms (we can negotiate the exact SLAs).

Next steps:
1) Confirm you want to proceed with the 25k-credit pilot and target dates.
2) Share a small sample of request traces (anonymized) so we can run a quick prefix-hit-rate projection.

Cheers,
Mateo
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@lumensoft.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LumenSoft Procurement <procurement@lumensoft.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit — pilot packaging and recommended technical guardrails

Thanks Mateo — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions before we loop legal: 

1) Quantization: our models are finetuned variants with several custom layers. Do you have a recommended checklist for safe int8 rollout (specific tests + expected failure modes)? Our concern is hallucinations spiking on certain prompts.

2) KV cache: our sessions are typically 3–6 turns with frequent role switching; is the 35% hit-rate threshold you mentioned conservative for this pattern?

3) Pricing: procurement asked for an upfront view of potential discounts if we convert to a 12-month committed plan after the pilot (they want ranges). Can you include tiered discount bands?

We’re happy to share anonymized traces — I can put together a small sample. Also, can we schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive with your infra lead this week?

—Sarah
Head of Product, LumenSoft
[Procurement: procurement@lumensoft.com]

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Optimize toolkit — pilot packaging and recommended technical guardrails

Looping in Hannah for commercial posture + legal cadence. Quick summary and suggested response to Sarah:

- Quantization checklist (proposal):
  * Baseline run on the dev prompt-set (A/B int8 vs fp16) with automated quality diff metrics (EM/ROUGE/LLR-based hallucination signal).
  * Per-layer sensitivity scan — mark the top 2 sensitive attention layers to keep in fp16 if needed.
  * Fallback policy: on drift > X% we automatically route to fp16 variant until retrain/calibration completes.

- KV cache threshold note: 35% was a conservative round number; given short sessions and role switching, we should instrument a live sampling job — if observed hit-rate >25% we still see material benefit because many of their tokens are repeated system prompts and templates. Recommend we ask for sample traces and we’ll run a quick projection (I can run this once Mateo drops the sample to our infra sandbox).

- Commercial concessions: propose offering the 25k pilot credits + 1 week of SRE support (as Mateo listed) and commit to a conversion discount framework if they convert to 12 months: 
  * Commit bands: 10% (>= $50k/mo equivalent), 15% (>= $100k/mo), 20% (>= $200k/mo).
  * If procurement needs a firm MSA change, we can provide the flex terms in redwood_terms_flex.docx — legal will need 3 business days to review.

Recommended reply: acknowledge the quantization risks and offer the technical deep-dive this week. Offer to intake anonymized traces and promise a projection within 48 hours. For procurement, include the commit band ranges and say final pricing will be in the SOW.

I’ve attached a short latency note that supports the KV recommendations. If you want, I can draft a short commercial one-pager to share directly with procurement.

Camila
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: kvcache_latency_report.pdf (PDF, 82KB)]

Commercial update (formalizing the offer):
- 3-month pilot, 25,000 pilot credits applied as discussed.
- 1 week dedicated SRE support during ramp.
- Conversion discount bands (if you convert within 30 days of pilot completion): 10% / 15% / 20% by commit band as Camila outlined.

Quantization rollout plan (high level):
- Step 1: calibration & A/B tests on dev prompt-set (we’ll provide scripts).
- Step 2: per-layer sensitivity scan — keep top 1–2 sensitive layers fp16 if needed.
- Step 3: deploy int8 in canary (5% traffic) + monitoring hooks that measure hallucination-indicator metrics; rollback to fp16 on threshold breach.

KV cache approach:
- Please send 48–72 hours of anonymized traces (we’ll provide a small ingestion script). We’ll return a hit-rate projection + expected cost delta within 48 hours of receipt.

I’ve attached the redwood flex terms for procurement to review. If this is acceptable I’ll send a DocuSign SOW for signature and we’ll kick off the technical intake.

Link to shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-lumensoft-pricing

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
